data.name: Orc Attack: Flatulent Rebellion
data.detailed_description:
Fart or die in this hack-and-slash action game, where fun-loving Orcs battle pollution loving Humans in a humorous fantasy setting. Orcs have become victims of brutal Human expansion, as they are carelessly poisoning the environment. Now, four trained Orc heroes are retaliating with a Not-So-Silent yet very deadly plan. In either single-player or up to four-player co-op, you will take on the role of Orcs, each wielding a unique gaseous ability, and then take the fight to the Humans in a stinky, fart-filled romp. Hilarious enemies and highly tuned combat make for a joyous experience that really is worth sharing. While the comedic storyline and the striking 3D world make it even more memorable. Gross but charming protagonists add the final flourish with flatulent group attacks and nasty killer moves for up to four players.

Key Features


  • Cooperative combat and dirty mode reward players for working together.
  • Four player local and online multiplayer.
  • Four campaigns comprise 25 epic missions.
  • 30+ enemies types including bosses
  • Raid, pillage, and plunder human camps, collect gold to buy improved weapons and armor.
  • Set free the orc prisoners to add them to your horde
  • Play as any of the 8 Orc warriors.

reviews.review:
Orc Attack: Flatulent Rebellion is an unusual hack-and-slash adventure that builds its entire identity around crude comedy, cartoon fantasy, and cooperative action. Developed by Casual Brothers Ltd. and published by Casual Brothers, the game was released on May 15, 2014. Its concept immediately separates it from conventional fantasy adventures because the orcs are not portrayed as invading monsters. Instead, they are the victims of aggressive human expansion and environmental pollution. The humans have contaminated their homeland, and a group of trained orc warriors decides to fight back using weapons, physical strength, and some particularly unpleasant biological abilities.

The environmental premise gives the otherwise ridiculous story a surprisingly coherent foundation. Human activity has damaged the natural world, turning the orcs into unlikely defenders of their territory. Rather than treating this theme seriously, the game transforms ecological retaliation into slapstick comedy. Flatulence becomes both a running joke and an actual weapon. It is an intentionally immature approach, but the game commits completely to the idea instead of using toilet humor as an occasional gimmick. Whether this succeeds will largely depend on the player's tolerance for fart jokes, burping, exaggerated bodily functions, and deliberately disgusting characters.

Gameplay follows the structure of an accessible 3D beat-'em-up. Players control an orc and battle groups of human enemies through melee-focused encounters. Traditional attacks are combined with gaseous abilities and more ridiculous special moves, creating combat that feels intentionally chaotic rather than technically sophisticated. The controls and fighting system are designed to make jumping into the action relatively straightforward. Consequently, the game is more concerned with immediate entertainment and crowd fighting than complicated combos or demanding character-action mechanics.

Cooperative play is one of its strongest ideas. Orc Attack supports single-player as well as multiplayer for up to four participants, and its mechanics clearly benefit from having several orcs causing destruction simultaneously. Cooperative combat and the appropriately named Dirty Mode encourage teamwork, while group attacks make the flatulence concept part of the multiplayer design rather than merely a visual joke. Shared or split-screen functionality also complements the party-game qualities of the experience. The resulting chaos can be entertaining with friends because players are simultaneously attacking enemies, using special abilities, and contributing to increasingly absurd situations.

There is considerably more campaign content than the intentionally silly premise might suggest. Four campaigns contain a total of 25 missions, while more than 30 enemy types, including bosses, provide opposition along the way. Players can raid human camps, collect gold, and spend their earnings on improved weapons and armor. Orc prisoners can also be rescued and added to the growing horde. These mechanics establish a basic progression loop in which combat leads to resources and stronger equipment, giving players reasons to explore stages and continue developing their characters rather than simply rushing from one encounter to another.

Eight playable orc warriors further expand the available variety. Different characters possess distinctive gaseous abilities, giving players opportunities to experiment and making cooperative teams more interesting. Equipment improvements can gradually strengthen a preferred warrior, while the different abilities help prevent every playable character from feeling completely interchangeable. The progression is not comparable to a deep role-playing game, but it provides enough customization to support the arcade-oriented combat system.

Presentation is another area where the game's personality becomes obvious. Its fantasy world uses colorful, exaggerated 3D visuals instead of pursuing realism. The orcs are grotesque yet intentionally cartoonish, while enemies and combat animations fit the slapstick atmosphere. The graphics naturally reveal the game's age today, but the stylized artistic direction has held up better than a realistic presentation probably would have. The exaggerated designs also make the frequent violence and gore feel more comedic than disturbing, although the Steam description appropriately warns about frequent violence, gore, and general mature content.

The greatest weakness is repetition. Once the novelty of defeating humans with bizarre bodily attacks wears off, the underlying gameplay becomes much more conventional. Fighting crowds, collecting resources, upgrading equipment, rescuing prisoners, and progressing through stages can provide steady entertainment, but the combat lacks the complexity necessary to remain consistently engaging for players seeking a demanding hack-and-slash experience. Playing alone can emphasize these limitations because much of the game's personality comes from the chaos produced when multiple players cooperate.

Its humor presents an equally significant limitation. The game does not gradually introduce its crude comedy or use it sparingly. Flatulence is fundamental to the story, characters, attacks, cooperative mechanics, and overall presentation. Players who find that style of humor amusing may appreciate the commitment, while those who dislike toilet jokes will probably become tired of the concept quickly. There is little middle ground because the developers deliberately built the experience around its most ridiculous characteristic.

Despite those shortcomings, Orc Attack deserves recognition for having a distinctive identity. Many inexpensive fantasy action games rely on familiar medieval settings and predictable heroes, whereas this one reverses the usual human-versus-orc relationship and combines environmental satire with juvenile comedy. Its combination of eight warriors, four campaigns, 25 missions, numerous enemies, bosses, equipment upgrades, prisoner rescues, and four-player cooperative action gives the game a respectable amount of substance beneath its deliberately foolish exterior. Steam achievements provide another incentive for players interested in completing additional objectives.

Orc Attack: Flatulent Rebellion ultimately works best as a lighthearted cooperative brawler rather than a serious action adventure. Its combat is accessible but repetitive, its progression systems are useful without being especially deep, and its humor is memorable precisely because it refuses to exercise restraint. With friends who appreciate crude comedy, the cooperative battles can produce genuinely entertaining moments. As a solo experience, its mechanical limitations become easier to notice. Casual Brothers Ltd. nevertheless created something recognizable and unusual instead of another anonymous fantasy hack-and-slash game. 

Rating: 6/10
